stem: The equation of a line, having inclination \(120^\circ\) with positive direction of \(X\)-axis, which is at a distance of 3 units from the origin is
_derivation: Slope = tan 120 = -sqrt(3), so line is sqrt(3)x + y + c = 0. Distance from origin |c|/sqrt(3+1) = |c|/2 = 3 => c = +/-6, i.e. sqrt(3)x + y +/- 6 = 0.

stem: A line passes through \((2,2)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(3x+y=3\). Its \(y\)-intercept is
_note: The book prints the word as 'y-interecpt' (typo for 'y-intercept'); transcribed with the correct spelling.
_derivation: Slope of 3x+y=3 is -3, so perpendicular slope = 1/3. y - 2 = (1/3)(x - 2) => y = x/3 + 4/3, y-intercept 4/3.
